link.description: The link itself: only right after making it.

live.description: Whether it can still let someone new in.

search.description: Part of a name; empty or absent for all.

name.description: Also the ones the site doesn't know yet.

AdminRole.description: A role as the roles listing has it, with its permissions.

AdminRolePage.description: One page of a listing, and how many there are in all.

AdminRoleRef.description: A role without its permissions: `GET /api/admin/roles/all`, for the pickers.

AdminUserRole.description: A role as the user listing has it.

ArcaneMe.description:
`GET /api/arcane/me`: always answered, so the extension can tell "logged out" from
"server down".

ArcaneServerMsg.description: A message from `/ws/arcane`, or an event's data on `/api/arcane/rolls` (always a roll).

oneOf.description: What was seen in one camera frame.

frame_ms.description: How long reading the frame took.

frame_seq.description: The number of the camera frame this answers (1, 2, … per connection).

oneOf.description: The dice in view have settled into a new roll (or one re-read).

frame_seq.description: The camera frame it settled on.

roll_id.description: Kept when the same dice are read again.

total.description: The sum (a d10's "0" counts 10); `None` unless every die was read.

ArkCommand.description: What the Ark server can be told to do: the commands auth accepts.

count.description: `None` when the game server doesn't say (it is offline).

Bootstrap.description: Who is looking at the page: what `GET /api/session` answers.

Code.description: A one-time code from an emailed link or an invite link.

Confirmed.description: An address confirmed with an emailed code: whose.

Deleted.description: How many shared rolls were deleted.

Deletion.description: What a delete-account link is for, before it is used.

Detection.description: One die found in a frame.

value.description: The face it shows ("0" is the d10 zero).

x1.description: The box, as fractions of the frame.

Done.description:
After resetting a password or deleting an account: whether this browser's session was that
account's and has been logged out.

EnshroudedActionName.description:
A command as auth stored it: one this site sends, or a name it doesn't know (from an older
or newer auth), which still deserializes.

EnshroudedCommand.description:
Restart, or force an update: `update` waits until nobody is online, `update_now`
disconnects the players.

sessions.description: How long each player has been connected, in seconds (the game sends no names).

oneOf.description: The process runs but the world isn't loaded yet.
Neither the server nor its control port answers.

EnshroudedStatus.description: The Enshrouded server as the panel (`/enshrouded`) shows it: auth's `StatusResp`, passed on.

can_control.description: Whether Restart / Force update can be sent right now.

latest_build_at.description: When Steam last published a build (unix seconds).

next_command_at.description: When the next command may be sent (unix seconds), while that is in the future.

players.description: `None` when the server doesn't answer the query.

update_pending.description: Steam has a build the server doesn't run.

update_queued.description: Someone asked for an update that waits for the server to be empty.

uptime_secs.description: Seconds the server process has been running.

ErrorCode.description:
What kind of failure an [`ApiError`] is: for the code paths that branch on it. The rest is
in the message. Clients send the user to the login page on `logged_out` only, never on a
401 alone: a wrong password is a 401 too (`invalid`).

FlagRequest.description:
`POST /api/arcane/flag`: the latest roll read wrong, with the user's corrections (one per
die, left to right; `null` for one left empty).

ForgotPassword.description: `POST /api/password/forgot`: a username or an email address.

frame_ms.description: How long reading the frame took.

frame_seq.description: The number of the camera frame this answers (1, 2, … per connection).

KnownPermission.description:
The permissions the site knows. Every permission check uses this closed set, so TypeScript
gets a literal union.

LoggedIn.description: A login or registration that succeeded.

NewInvite.description:
`POST /api/admin/invites`: a link that gives `role_id`, working for `days` days and for up
to `max_uses` people (`None`: any number).

Opened.description: What opening an invite link did.

oneOf.description: The logged-in user now has `role` (or already had it through this link).
Logged out: the invite is kept until they log in or sign up.

PagePath.description:
A page's path. Deserializing anything else (another site, an API path, a page that
doesn't exist) fails.

Permission.description:
A permission name from auth, which may have permissions the site doesn't know yet: those
deserialize as `Other` instead of failing. Only for showing names; checks use
[`KnownPermission`].

Registration.description: `POST /api/session/register`: a new account, logged in at once.

frame_seq.description: The camera frame it settled on.

roll_id.description: Kept when the same dice are read again.

total.description: The sum (a d10's "0" counts 10); `None` unless every die was read.

box.description: As fractions of the frame: [x1, y1, x2, y2].

value.description: "1".."20" ("0" is the d10 zero); `None` when it couldn't be read confidently.

available.description: False when the training-data store isn't configured on this server.

Viewer.description: The logged-in user, as the page shows them.

permissions.description: Only the ones the site knows; empty when auth can't be reached.

shown_name.description: The display name, or the username when there is none.
